features.title: Writable ext2 and later ext4
features.current: Classic ext2 root and data volumes support persistent files, external xattrs and file capabilities, shared EA copy-on-write, direct/indirect and sparse storage, mount policy, metadata operations, host fsck, and fresh kernel reboot verification. Writable checked dirty mounts reconcile in-range free counters and reclaim validated, unreferenced deletion-marked inodes. A retired file or symlink with one validated name and matching change/deletion times can retain its name and contents or target. An empty retired directory can retain one live parent name and restore only that parent's bounded link contribution. Full allocation, inode, attribute and directory checks precede correction, followed by strict validation of the staged result. Nonempty retired directories, multiple retirements under one parent, unrelated link errors and cleared inode bodies remain rejected. Initial internal-journal support replays committed records and logs complete data and metadata operations before updating their home blocks, with explicit feature admission and stale-record crash controls. Dirty journaled mounts reclaim validated unreferenced retirement records, including read-only requests on writable hardware, while keeping free counters and names strict. Journal sizing and complete device-failure acceptance remain required. ACLs, inline/ext4 attributes, orphan chains, advanced formats and general recovery after power loss remain planned.

features.title: VFS, mounts, and pseudo filesystems
features.current: RAM and classic ext2 mounts, Linux path/no-follow/descriptor xattrs, filesystem dispatch, directory identity, read-only policy, mount-aware statfs, rename, links, pipes, and selected synthetic device metadata work. O_PATH retains file, directory and no-follow symlink identity for metadata, duplication, relative lookup and empty-path readlink while rejecting data I/O and mapping. Closing a path descriptor preserves POSIX locks; ordinary descriptor closure releases the process's inode locks. Local advisory flock supports canonical inode ownership, descriptor lifetime, retained waits, and tested signal restart on the single-CPU kernel. Procfs provides process/thread status, enumeration, caller-relative links, description-owned reads and retained inode lifetime. Stat records include actual process/thread birth ticks, and a secure UUID identifies each initialized kernel boot; accounting and complete procfs remain unfinished.
